A new type of "high-level programming language" that seems really worth trying to make, is a language that gets compiled to Lean (or HOL, or...) that is specifically about making it as friendly as possible for a human to read definitions and theorems.

Not the proofs - as all

It really is a step change in how you approach getting work out of a system, requiring as much thinking as moving from GPT-4o to GPT-5/o3. And, of course, we don't have a lot of accumulated knowledge or clear studies about how to prompt these more powerful systems yet.

“Geologists communicated in English; and they could name things in a manner that sent shivers through the bones"

Not a whiff of LLM feel, despite the em-dashes & period-separated lists. We focus too much on the surface stuff of what makes AI-writing samey, rather than the craft. https://t.co/rNOlE2i34B

输出价格有所降低，有优势，能力比3.5 Flash 有所提升，大幅超越了3.1 Pro https://t.co/hlz480m7uA

相比上一代 3.5 Flash，它在处理多步骤复杂任务时需要的计算步骤和工具调用更少，输出 Token 消耗减少了 17%，价格也降低了

减少了乱改代码和死循环的情况，代码质量更高、更稳定（DeepSWE 测试得分从 37% 提升到 49%）。
